topography.fall: Ground falls AWAY from Fort Foote Road toward the rear (north/north-west) by roughly 6-9 ft, with contours tightly packed along the frontage — a steep bank from the road down into the lots. This is what makes rear walkout basements work and it makes driveway grade the binding constraint (Sec. 32-151 Table 4).

topography._floodplainCaveat: NO FLOODPLAIN LINE IS LABELLED ON ANY OF THE THREE SCANS. The file named 'floodplain topo' carries unlabelled red, teal and black overlay lines flanking the drainage channel. They are PLAUSIBLY a floodplain or stream-buffer limit and are NOT drawn or labelled as such here. Confirm against the PG floodplain layer or the FEMA FIRM panel before any floodplain line goes on a sheet.

naturalResourceInventory.whyOneIsRequired: PG County requires an NRI where regulated environmental features are present. The Stream Center and Drainage layer maps channel through ALL FOUR lots (lot 53 ~98 ft, lot 54 ~195 ft, lot 55 ~425 ft, lot 56 ~42 ft), steep slopes at or above 25% cover 23-37% of each lot, and ZS 'Zekiah and Issue soils, frequently flooded' covers 94% of lot 54. An NRI with a field-delineated stream, its Primary Management Area buffer, wetlands and specimen trees is the gate on siting anything here, and it is not on file.
naturalResourceInventory.nextStep: Commission an NRI for the four lots. Until the stream and its buffer are delineated, no dwelling footprint on lots 54 or 55 can be shown as compliant.

combinedConstraint.note: Union of slope>=25%, GI Regulated Area and ZS frequently-flooded soils, as a screen only.
combinedConstraint.warning: This is a DESKTOP SCREEN, not a buildable-area determination. The GI Regulated Area is a planning overlay rather than a prohibition, the NRCS soils are coarse, and NRI-033-2015 governs. It does however say plainly that siting four dwellings here is constrained and needs the NRI and a stream-buffer determination before any footprint is placed.
